items.note: The newsletter band shows the 'nope' input with a red border and an error line below it: an icon plus 'Enter a valid email address, like name@example.com', so the person knows what to fix. The ink Subscribe button sits lifted on its hard offset shadow, and the only pink action is the hero CTA, which is off this part of the page.

In dark, the input sits on a raised dark fill with a red border, the red icon-and-text error line stays readable on the black ground, and Subscribe is the paper-filled inverse button with a light offset shadow. This follows the spec's dark mapping.

At phone width the form stacks into one column: label, a full-width input with a red border, the ink Subscribe button, then the wrapped error line with its icon. Nothing is clipped and the message sits right under the action.

The form is replaced by a raised confirmation card with an ink border and a hard offset shadow, holding a pink check icon and 'Thanks for subscribing. New posts will arrive at reader@example.com.' It's clear and built like the spec's toast card.
Same confirmation card on a dark raised fill with a light border and offset shadow. The pink check sits next to the sentence, so the status isn't shown by color alone, and the text reads clearly.
The confirmation card spans the column under the newsletter heading, with the check icon and the two-line message wrapping cleanly inside the bordered, shadowed card.

Under the yellow 'More posts' band, the search field shows the pink focus halo and a clear-x, the count reads 'Showing 0 of 6 posts', and the empty area holds a large blue magnifier sticker, 'No posts match these filters', a hint line and a pink 'Clear filters' button. The hero CTA switched to a ghost button, so only one pink action is visible.

In dark, the band stays yellow with ink text, the dark search field has its pink halo, and the magnifier sticker has a light outline. The single pink Clear filters button and the ghost hero CTA keep the one-pink rule.

At phone width the focused search field with the halo fills the band, the pill strip scrolls off the right edge as the spec asks, and the magnifier sticker, message, hint and pink Clear filters are centered below without clipping.
Keyboard focus is on the ink 'Home' current-page pill in the header: a 2px ring at an offset, following the pill's shape. It's clearly visible and not the browser default.
In dark, the paper-filled Home pill carries the pink-toned focus ring at an offset, clearly separated from the pill and readable on the black header.
At phone width the focused Home pill shows the same offset ring inside the header without being clipped by the header edge.

The hero stickers are a pink coin with a plus glyph and an extruded yellow rim, a yellow star, a pink pencil, a white speech bubble with ink lines, and a document with a pink folded corner on the yellow featured tile. All are flat fills with a heavy ink outline, tilted and cropped at the edges like the reference's hero coins, and no drawing repeats.

The article figure is a rounded frame holding a yellow ellipse with a pink and a teal rounded rectangle. It is built to the sticker recipe (heavy ink outline, band fills), but it reads as abstract shapes rather than its caption's subject, a board of many buttons grouped into a few jobs.

The figure shows a blue page with squiggles, a pink arrow, and a white page with clean ink lines: a clear before-and-after rewrite in 3 shapes, with flat fills and ink outlines that read well at article width.

Frame strip m1 shows the hero coin and star under the scroll-bound linear drift (static while the page isn't scrolling, no bounce or scale), and m2 shows the tag wall moving left at a steady linear speed across the frames. That matches the spec's two decorative loops, and nothing else loops.

findings.summary: The design-system article figure is a generic composition (two rounded rectangles on a yellow ellipse inside a frame) that doesn't depict its subject, many buttons grouped into a few jobs. The spec asks for a figure that shows what it stands for.
